rounds.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
rounds.note: First conditional: if + present simple, will + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: If I ___ more money, I'd buy a bigger flat.
rounds.note: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: If she had left earlier, she ___ the train.
rounds.note: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: If you heat ice, it ___.
rounds.note: Zero conditional: if + present, present. It describes a general truth.

rounds.prompt: If I had studied medicine, I ___ a doctor now.
rounds.note: Mixed conditional: a past condition with a present result.

rounds.prompt: ___ you need help, just call me.
rounds.note: Should + subject + infinitive replaces if in a formal first conditional.

rounds.prompt: ___ I known about the traffic, I'd have left earlier.
rounds.note: Had + subject + past participle replaces if in the third conditional.

rounds.prompt: You can stay here ___ you keep quiet.
rounds.note: As long as = only if.

rounds.prompt: Set an alarm; ___, you'll oversleep.
rounds.note: Otherwise = or else, if you don't. It starts a new clause.

rounds.prompt: If I ___ you, I'd apologise.
rounds.note: In advice with If I ___ you, use were.

rounds.prompt: ___ you won the lottery, what would you do?
rounds.note: Suppose / supposing = imagine that. It works like if in unreal questions.

rounds.prompt: If he ___ so rude, she wouldn't have left.
rounds.note: Third conditional needs the past perfect in the if clause.

rounds.prompt: If I ___ (know) his number, I would call him.
rounds.note: Second conditional: if + past simple.

rounds.prompt: If we ___ (leave) now, we'll arrive by six.
rounds.note: First conditional: if + present simple.

rounds.prompt: If she ___ (not / miss) the bus, she wouldn't have been late.
rounds.note: Third conditional: if + past perfect.

rounds.prompt: I wouldn't have gone if I ___ (know) it was so far.
rounds.note: If + past perfect, even when the if clause comes second.

rounds.prompt: If I ___ (be) you, I'd take the job.
rounds.note: Were is the standard form; was is accepted in informal speech.

rounds.prompt: Provided that you ___ (pay) on time, there's no extra charge.
rounds.note: Provided that + present simple, not will.

rounds.prompt: If I hadn't eaten so much, I ___ (not / feel) ill now.
rounds.note: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

rounds.prompt: Had I ___ (know) earlier, I would have helped.
rounds.note: Had + subject + past participle.

rounds.prompt: If you ___ (mix) red and blue, you get purple.
rounds.note: Zero conditional: present + present for facts.

rounds.prompt: If they ___ (not / cancel) the flight, we would be in Rome now.
rounds.note: Mixed conditional: past perfect in the if clause, would + infinitive in the result.

rounds.context: A real possibility in the future.
rounds.line: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay in.
rounds.note: If + present simple, will.

rounds.line: If I ___ rich, I'd travel the world.
rounds.note: If + past simple, would.

rounds.context: An unreal situation in the past.
rounds.line: If we ___ earlier, we'd have got seats.
rounds.note: If + past perfect, would have.

rounds.line: If you cool water to 0°C, it ___.
rounds.note: Zero conditional: present + present.

rounds.line: You can go ___ you're back by ten.
rounds.note: As long as = only if.

rounds.line: Leave now; ___, you'll miss the train.
rounds.note: Otherwise = or else.

rounds.line: ___ you need more information, please contact us.
rounds.note: Should + subject replaces if in formal writing.

rounds.context: A past condition with a present result.
rounds.line: If I'd taken that job, I ___ in Paris now.
rounds.note: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: If + present simple, will + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: If I were you + would.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: As long as + present simple.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Had + subject + past participle, would have.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
rounds.note: Unless + present simple, will.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: If I win, I'll buy you dinner.
If I won, I'd buy you dinner.
If I will win, I'll buy you dinner.
If I win, I will buy you dinner.
rounds.answer: If I will win, I'll buy you dinner.
rounds.note: No will in the if clause.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: If I had known, I would have told you.
If I knew, I would have told you.
Had I known, I would have told you.
If I'd known, I'd have told you.
rounds.answer: If I knew, I would have told you.
rounds.note: Third conditional: the if clause needs the past perfect.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: Unless you study, you won't pass.
If you don't study, you won't pass.
Unless you don't study, you won't pass.
You won't pass unless you study.
rounds.answer: Unless you don't study, you won't pass.
rounds.note: Unless already means if … not, so it can't take a negative.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: If it rains, we'll cancel the picnic.
If it rains, cancel the picnic.
If it rains, we would cancel the picnic.
If it rains, we might cancel the picnic.
rounds.answer: If it rains, we would cancel the picnic.
rounds.note: After if + present, use will, might, can or an imperative, not would.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: Should you need help, call me.
Had I known, I would have told you.
Would I known, I'd have told you.
rounds.answer: Would I known, I'd have told you.
rounds.note: Inversion uses had, were or should, never would.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: I'll lend you the money provided that you pay me back.
I'll lend you the money as long as you pay me back.
I'll lend you the money providing you'll pay me back.
I'll lend you the money if you pay me back.
rounds.answer: I'll lend you the money providing you'll pay me back.
rounds.note: Providing takes the present simple, not will.

rounds.prompt: Real possibility or unreal situation?
items: If it rains, we'll stay in.
If you heat ice, it melts.
If I finish early, I'll call you.
If I were a bird, I'd fly.
If she had more time, she'd help.
If we had left earlier, we'd have arrived.
rounds.note: Zero and first conditionals are real; second and third are imagined.

rounds.prompt: Second or third conditional?
items: If I knew, I'd say.
If I were you, I'd go.
If she had time, she'd come.
If I'd known, I'd have said.
If she had come, we'd have won.
If they hadn't left, we'd have met.
rounds.note: Past simple points to the second; past perfect points to the third.

rounds.prompt: Alternative to if, or inversion?
items: provided that
as long as
suppose
had I known
should you need
were I you
rounds.note: Inversion drops if and moves had, were or should to the front.

rounds.prompt: What follows the if clause?
items: If I were rich,
If she knew,
If it snowed,
If I had known,
If they had won,
If he hadn't left,
rounds.note: Past simple leads to would; past perfect leads to would have.

rounds.prompt: Zero or first conditional?
items: If you boil water, it evaporates.
If metal gets hot, it expands.
If you press this, it stops.
If it's sunny, we'll go out.
If I see him, I'll tell him.
If you fail, you'll retake it.
rounds.note: Zero states facts; first predicts a result in the future.

rounds.prompt: Match each conditional to its use.
rounds.note: Four conditionals, four uses.

rounds.prompt: Match each conditional to its structure.
rounds.note: The tense in the if clause decides the type.

rounds.prompt: Match each linker to its meaning.
rounds.note: Alternatives to if.

rounds.prompt: Match each inversion to its full form.
rounds.note: Inversion is a formal way to drop if.

rounds.prompt: If you aren't on time, we'll leave without you.
rounds.stem: We'll leave without you ___ on time.
rounds.note: If … not → unless.

rounds.prompt: I don't have a car, so I can't give you a lift.
rounds.stem: ___ a car, I could give you a lift.
rounds.note: Real fact → unreal condition: if + past simple.

rounds.prompt: She didn't study, so she failed.
rounds.stem: If she had studied, she ___ failed.
rounds.note: Third conditional result: would have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: We didn't know about the party, so we didn't go.
rounds.stem: ___ about the party, we would have gone.
rounds.note: If we had known → Had we known.

rounds.prompt: Call me if you need help.
rounds.note: If you need → Should you need.

rounds.prompt: You can borrow it only if you return it tomorrow.
rounds.stem: You can borrow it ___ it tomorrow.
rounds.note: Only if → as long as.

rounds.prompt: If you don't take a coat, you'll be cold.
rounds.note: If not → otherwise.

rounds.prompt: In your position, I'd accept the offer.
rounds.stem: If I ___ position, I'd accept the offer.
rounds.note: In your position → If I were in your position.

rounds.sentence: If I will see her, I'll tell her.
rounds.note: No will in the if clause.

rounds.sentence: If I would have known, I would have helped.
rounds.note: Third conditional: if + past perfect, never would have.

rounds.sentence: If I have more time, I would learn Spanish.
rounds.note: Second conditional: if + past simple.

rounds.sentence: I'll lend you the money providing you will pay it back.
rounds.note: Providing + present simple.

rounds.sentence: If he had studied, he would passed.
rounds.note: Third conditional result: would have + past participle.

rounds.sentence: If I were rich, I will buy a boat.
rounds.note: Second conditional result: would + infinitive.

rounds.sentence: Had I would known, I'd have come.
rounds.note: Inversion: had + subject + past participle.

rounds.sentence: If I had gone to bed earlier, I would be tired now.
rounds.note: Mixed conditional: the meaning needs a negative result.
